sources.title: Water resources planning guideline
sources.role: Official WRMP guidance publication for water companies and regional groups.
sources.facts: Published 24 February 2021; updated 16 June 2026; requires companies to prepare and maintain water resources management plans.
sources.origin: Environment Agency, Natural Resources Wales and Ofwat.
sources.guard: A WRMP framework does not prove connection capacity, a supply agreement, scheme funding or delivery at a site.

sources.title: Water resources planning guideline: detailed guidance
sources.role: Detailed 2026 guidance for supply, demand, uncertainty, options and best-value planning.
sources.facts: Updated 16 June 2026; covers national, regional and company planning and annual review of WRMPs.
sources.origin: Environment Agency, Natural Resources Wales and Ofwat.
sources.guard: Forecasts and options are planning evidence, not a binding capacity reservation, connection date or construction commitment.

sources.title: National Framework for Water Resources 2025: planning and abstraction licensing
sources.role: Environment Agency national framework section on water rights and planning.
sources.facts: Updated 15 April 2026; explains high-level allocation of abstraction rights and environmental protection considerations.
sources.guard: The national framework does not grant an abstraction licence, reserve water, or confirm a scheme is environmentally acceptable.

sources.title: Check if you need a licence to abstract water
sources.facts: Published 31 March 2022; updated 2 July 2026; explains when abstraction from surface and groundwater may require a licence.
sources.guard: Guidance does not prove an exemption applies, a licence exists, licensed volume is available or conditions are satisfied.

sources.title: Groundwater source protection zones
sources.role: Environment Agency explanation and mapping of groundwater source protection zones.
sources.facts: Published 1 August 2019; updated 1 August 2024; describes SPZ definitions and modelled travel-time protection areas.
sources.guard: An SPZ map is modelled screening evidence and does not prove contamination, permit refusal, exact geology or site outcome.

sources.title: Protect groundwater and prevent groundwater pollution
sources.role: Environment Agency groundwater protection and permission guidance.
sources.facts: Published 14 March 2017; updated 17 July 2025; covers pollution risks, permissions and groundwater vulnerability.
sources.guard: Protection guidance does not prove a development is compliant, permitted or free from groundwater risk.

sources.title: Guidelines for statutory Drainage and Wastewater Management Plans
sources.role: Multi-regulator guidance for statutory drainage and wastewater planning.
sources.facts: Published 20 May 2025; explains preparation, publication and maintenance of statutory DWMPs.
sources.origin: Defra, Environment Agency, Ofwat, Welsh Government and Natural Resources Wales.
sources.guard: A DWMP is strategic and does not prove sewer capacity, connection approval, reinforcement completion or occupancy readiness.

sources.title: Discharges to surface water and groundwater: environmental permits
sources.role: Environment Agency guidance on discharge permits and new-development foul drainage.
sources.facts: Current guidance covers discharge permits, trade effluent, public foul sewer connection and early consultation for development.
sources.guard: Planning permission or early consultation does not itself provide a discharge permit, trade-effluent consent or network capacity.
